subject: Pilot extension — incremental credits vs pro-rata days (TaskWell)
messages:
From: Olivia Marsh <olivia@taskwell.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow on pilot runway — can we top up or convert?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the workshop yesterday — the model latency improvements are already visible in our sandbox runs. We're coming up against the end of our 30-day pilot and the team would like a short runway so we can validate a larger prompt set.

Two options on the table internally:
- Buy an extra 14 pro‑rata days on the existing time-box (preferred for our cadence), or
- Convert to an "incremental credits" bucket (X tokens) that we can draw from while we ramp.

From TaskWell's side, pro‑rata days are easier operationally but finance prefers a single invoice/credit top‑up. Do you have a recommended approach from Redwood's side? If we proceed with days we'd like the addendum to be minimal (no SLA changes) and signed by Friday.

Attaching a short note on our expected burn pattern.

Appreciate your help — Olivia

Attachment: taskwell_burn_preview.csv (spreadsheet stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Marsh <olivia@taskwell.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow on pilot runway — can we top up or convert?

Hi Olivia — great to hear the sandbox is showing improvement.

Short answer: both are workable. A quick note on tradeoffs so you can share with finance/legal:

Option A — Pro‑rata days
- We append a 14‑day addendum to the existing pilot. No rate changes, no SLA changes.
- Operationally simple: we continue to route to the same dedicated pilot pool and keep the same model pin.
- Internal impact: requires a short contract addendum (1 page) and a prorated invoice.

Option B — Incremental credits bucket
- We issue a one‑time credit invoice (tokens billed up front). Credits give you flexibility across bursts but can complicate month‑end reconciliation for finance.
- Allows us to keep a single invoice line item if that's important for procurement.

Logistics: I can draft the 1‑page addendum for pro‑rata days now (will attach as "mop_addendum_draft.docx"). Ben — can you confirm whether finance prefers the credit SKU or a prorated invoice for a 14‑day top‑up? Priyom — FYI in case we need a very small legal redline.

If TaskWell is OK with a simple days addendum we can route for signature and bill immediately. If you want credits, we can provide the SKU and a sample invoice today.

Thanks,
Soojin
--
Soojin Lee

Date: 2026-10-05T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow on pilot runway — can we top up or convert?

Heads up on finance preferences. For small, near‑term runway extensions our billing team prefers an invoice-based pro‑rata charge rather than issuing a credits bucket — it keeps revenue recognition straightforward and avoids credit accounting in our ledger.

If TaskWell signs the 14‑day addendum we can:
1) Issue a prorated invoice (NET 30) for the extra period,
2) Expedite provisioning so the additional days begin immediately after signature.

If legal needs a minor redline (e.g., termination language), Priyom can advise; otherwise this should be a low‑touch addendum.

I've added the HubSpot deal link below (TW-2147) and will prepare an invoice template for the prorate case.

Ben

Thanks, Soojin and Ben.

TaskWell will take Option A — pro‑rata 14 days. Our finance team prefers a single prorated invoice, so Ben's workflow fits us. Legal will only ask for the following tiny clarify: explicit statement that this addendum does not change data retention or access rights.

We can sign the 1‑page addendum today if you send the DocuSign link. We'd also be open to a 7% one‑time courtesy discount on the prorated charge if that helps expedite approval on our side (small ask given the short duration).

Olivia
Director of ML Platform, TaskWell
olivia@taskwell.io
